newsitem.title: USA: Sun says Q1 oper margin was record level.
newsitem.headline: Sun says Q1 oper margin was record level.

text.p: Sun Microsystems Inc executives said its first quarter pre-tax operating margin of 9.5 percent was a record level for the company's typically seasonall-weak September quarter.
"It was our strongest Q1 ever," said Scott McNealy.
Michael Lehman, Sun Microsystems chief financial officer, said, "operating income at 9.5 percent, reached its highest level ever for a Q1."
"Our first quarter is typically seasonally our weakest in the fiscal year and our fourth quarter is typically our strongest," he said.

He said that nearly one percentage point of gross margin improvement to 47.7 percent in the first quarter from 44.7 percent was related to decreased memory cost, while noting the company had recently memory product price reductions.

Lehman also said Sun had reclassified certain costs associated with people in SunService sales or marketing activities into selling, general and administrative expenses from cost of sales, adding about one point sequentially to the first quarter's gross margin and SG&A costs.

Lehman said backlogs improved, with net bookings up 20.3 percent from a year ago at $1.74 billion, but with backlog having fallen sequentially to $405.8 million at the end of September from a record $522.2 million three months earlier.
"We still have some room to improve lead times," he said, noting that its longest lead times of three to four weeks currently were down from levels of recent months.
"At this point, it is only certain UltraSPARC models that are in short supply," he said.
He noted that head count had grown by nearly 800 people, including about 230 on the Sparc business of Cray Research acquired on July 1.

"I would expect that our overall hiring rate would slow a bit throughout the year given where we are at the end of Q1, however we will continue to invest in the resources needed to grow the business," he said.
